goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Imported external HTML stored with cook_method: raw_html bypasses the cooking/sanitization pipeline and is rendered with raw post.cooked; RSS content in poll_feed is imported with zero sanitization, enabling stored XSS on the Discourse origin

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `:raw_html` cook method in `Post#cook` that returns `raw` and skips the normal cooking pipeline (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and sets `raw` to `absolutize_urls(url, contents)` where `contents` comes directly from RSS/Atom (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`), with no sanitization/whitelisting. The embed UI renders posts using `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, so any HTML/JS present in the imported feed content can be stored and rendered, enabling stored XSS on the Discourse origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The readability path's attribute whitelist still permits href="javascript:..." URLs which flow unmodified into raw-HTML posts

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `Readability::Document.new(..., attributes: %w[href src])` whitelists the presence of `href`/`src` attributes but does not enforce safe URL schemes in this diff. The resulting `doc.content` is then imported via `TopicEmbed.import`, creating a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, `:raw_html` returns `raw` unchanged (skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. As a result, an `<a href="javascript:...">` (or similar) coming from the readability path would flow into a raw-HTML post and be rendered unmodified, enabling XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb uses $redis.setnx followed by a separate $redis.expire which is not atomic; a crash between the calls leaves the retrieved:<url> key with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval; should use SET ... EX NX

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the code does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two distinct Redis commands with a failure window between them: if the process crashes or is killed after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the `retrieved:<url>` key will remain without a TTL and `setnx` will keep failing forever, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return true permanently and blocking retrieval for that URL. Using an atomic command like `SET key value NX EX 60` (or a transaction/Lua) would avoid this defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_retrieve invokes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside the RetrieveTopic worker, re-importing the entire feed on every first-time embed request instead of filtering for the requested embed_url

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously (not enqueued) before attempting `fetch_http`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` always fetches and parses the entire configured feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) and iterates `rss.items.each`, calling `TopicEmbed.import(...)` for every item. This is triggered by a single embed request (`RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#retrieve`) and is not filtered to the requested `@embed_url`, so a first-time embed lookup can cause a full feed import (and potentially creation/update of many topics) as a side effect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migrations use force: true which silently drops pre-existing tables in production, and CreateTopTopics is an already-released migration being retroactively edited causing existing and new installs to diverge

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `force: true` to `create_table` in two places: a new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` and (more importantly) it edits an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to change `create_table :top_topics` into `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing table before creating it, which can cause data loss if the migration is run against a DB where that table already exists (e.g., rerun/rollback/replay scenarios). Also, modifying a previously-existing migration file is verifiable in the diff and is generally problematic because it changes migration history for new installs vs environments that already ran the old version.

adjudication_records.issue_text: URI(url) in absolutize_urls can raise URI::InvalidURIError for URLs that passed the loose regex (e.g. with spaces or bad characters), crashing the job with no rescue in retrieve/poll paths

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In TopicEmbed.import, the only URL validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which accepts strings that start with http(s) but are not valid URIs (e.g. containing spaces or other invalid characters). `absolutize_urls` then calls `uri = URI(url)` with no rescue, so `URI::InvalidURIError` can be raised and will bubble up, crashing callers like `Jobs::PollFeed` (which passes `i.link`/`i.id` after a similarly loose check) and the retrieve path that ultimately calls `TopicEmbed.import`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true is on an unlimited-length string column; URLs routinely exceed MySQL index prefix limits causing migration failure, and no length limit is defined on the column

adjudication.rationale: In the migration, `embed_url` is declared as `t.string :embed_url, null: false` with no explicit `limit`, which in Rails maps to a VARCHAR(255) by default (not an unlimited-length string). Therefore the premise of an “unlimited-length string column” is incorrect as written. Also, the index is on this default-length string column; whether it exceeds MySQL index prefix limits depends on external factors (e.g., utf8mb4 and MySQL version), which are not established in the diff. The diff itself does not verifiably introduce a migration failure due to index length.

adjudication_records.issue_text: On the update path, embed.post may be nil if the post was deleted while the embed row remains, causing PostRevisor.new(nil) to crash and permanently break polling for that feed entry

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then (when the SHA1 differs) calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` without guarding against `post` being nil. Since the `topic_embeds` table has no shown foreign key constraint and the `belongs_to :post` association has no `dependent:` cleanup in this diff, it’s possible for the associated Post to be deleted while the `topic_embeds` row remains. In that case `embed.post` returns nil, `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will raise, and because the embed’s `content_sha1` is never updated the same feed entry can keep crashing on subsequent polls when content changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController#best will raise if the topic behind an existing TopicEmbed was deleted (TopicView.new on a stale topic_id)

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, the presence check is only `if topic_id`, where `topic_id` comes from `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` which simply plucks `:topic_id` from `topic_embeds`. There is no verification that the referenced Topic still exists before calling `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`. Since `topic_embeds` has no foreign key constraint and the diff doesn’t show any dependent-destroy/cascade cleanup, a stale TopicEmbed row could remain after a topic is deleted, causing `TopicView.new` to raise (e.g., record not found) when it tries to load the missing topic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus.thor removed the :category / -c option so existing import invocations using -c fail with an unknown-option error, and imported topics can no longer be targeted at a category

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the line `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` was removed, along with all logic that reads `options[:category]`, resolves a `category_id`, and passes it into `PostCreator` (`category: category_id`). The import path now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not accept/pass a category. Therefore any existing `disqus:import` invocation using `-c` will raise an unknown option error in Thor, and there is no longer a way in this task to target imported topics to a specific category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus.thor discards the original created_at from the disqus export

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the previous code created the first post/topic with `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`. The diff removes that and instead calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which flows into `TopicEmbed.import` and `PostCreator.new(...)` without passing any `created_at`. As a result, the imported topic’s initial post will use the default timestamp (now) rather than the Disqus thread’s original `created_at`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb defines feed_key but never uses it; the intended conditional/If-Modified-Since fetch was never implemented so the feed is fully re-downloaded every hour

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb there is a method `feed_key` that is never referenced anywhere in the diff, so it is dead/unused code. However, the proposed finding goes further by asserting an intended If-Modified-Since/conditional-fetch mechanism “was never implemented”; that intent is not verifiable from the diff alone. The job downloading/parsing the feed hourly via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is consistent with its scheduled behavior and not inherently a correctness bug introduced by the diff.

poll_feed_spec.rb requires the wrong file (jobs/regular/process_post instead of the poll_feed job), and there are no tests for the poll_feed parsing/import logic, TopicEmbed.import_remote, absolutize_urls error cases, the RetrieveTopic job, or the embed views

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the diff shows `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'`, but the job being tested is `Jobs::PollFeed` which is added in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb. That require is therefore pointing at the wrong file and does not explicitly load the code under test (and may mask load/order issues). The rest of the finding about missing tests for other components is more of a test-coverage request than a verifiable defect in the diff.
